efficiency_assessment.issue: Multiple count metrics (order_count, customer_count, restaurant_count, delivery_count, agent_count, payment_count, promotion_count, review_count, support_ticket_count) follow identical patterns with only the table name varying.
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Consider creating a parameterized count metric template or macro to reduce repetition and improve maintainability.

efficiency_assessment.issue: Several metrics have nearly identical descriptions that differ only in the entity name (e.g., "Total number of X registered on the platform").
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Standardize metric description templates to reduce verbosity while maintaining clarity.

efficiency_assessment.issue: Revenue metrics (total_revenue, subtotal_revenue, delivery_fee_revenue, tax_revenue, tip_revenue) use identical SUM aggregation patterns on different columns from the same orders table.
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Consider creating a base revenue CTE that computes all revenue components in a single scan, then reference it in individual metrics.

efficiency_assessment.issue: Monthly aggregation metrics (monthly_revenue, monthly_order_count) duplicate the DATE_TRUNC logic and could benefit from a shared time dimension.
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Introduce a reusable time dimension or date spine table to standardize time-series aggregations across all metrics.

efficiency_assessment.issue: Several metrics (orders_per_customer, revenue_per_customer, orders_per_restaurant) perform similar joins and could share a common base query.
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Refactor related metrics to use shared CTEs or views to reduce query complexity and improve performance.

efficiency_assessment.issue: Multiple metrics implement identical CASE WHEN division-by-zero checks.
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Create a reusable safe_divide function or macro to eliminate repetitive null-handling logic.
